On August 6th and 7th, 2026, the Cornell Digital Forestry Initiative
([CoDiFI](../codifi.qmd)) held its third annual training workshop, welcoming 28
participants from four states — Ohio, Pennsylvania, Maryland, and New York.
Attendees came from the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation,
the Cary Institute of Ecosystem Studies, SUNY ESF, Penn State, the Adirondack
League Club, the University of Maryland, The Nature Conservancy, and Cornell.

The workshop covered the fundamentals of digital forestry tools — uncrewed
aerial vehicles (UAVs), terrestrial laser scanning (TLS), and mobile laser
scanning (MLS) — with a particular focus on lidar. Sessions ran from hands-on
field data collection through data processing to extracting the key biometric
information that feeds downstream analysis.

Participants left with practical knowledge of how to apply these tools across a
range of forestry contexts, from ecological research to applied forest
management.

Registration is already filling for next year. Please reach out to
[Xiangtao](mailto:xx286@cornell.edu) if you are interested in attending the 2027
workshop.
